paper.title: AGrail: A Lifelong Agent Guardrail with Effective and Adaptive Safety Detection
paper.central_claim: AGrail is a lifelong agent guardrail that adaptively generates and optimizes safety checks through a two-LLM (Analyzer/Executor) test-time-adaptation memory with optional tools, achieving strong ASR/benign trade-offs on task-specific and systemic risks and transferring across tasks.

signatures.object: memory of per-action safety-check lists (keys: step-back paraphrase of agent action; values: safety categories + checks)
signatures.information: agent action (+ optional environment observation), user request, agent spec, guard request / safety criteria, retrieved memory entry, toolbox; ground-truth safe/unsafe labels are not stated as part of the update loop (our_inference)
signatures.operation: Analyzer retrieves entry by key, revises/merges/adds checks; Executor deletes redundant/incorrect/over-blocking checks, validates remaining ones by tool or reasoning; any Unsafe result blocks the action; entry written back
signatures.output: updated memory m(t+1) and Safe/Unsafe verdict
signatures.conditions: TTA over a stream of agent actions; frozen-memory mode after training split
signatures.feedback: Executor LLM judgement plus tool outputs (OS environment code, permission checker, HTML detector)
signatures.selection_rule: Executor decides keep/delete; overwrite of existing entry if in_memory flag or key similarity > 0.8
signatures.persistence: memory dictionary persisted across actions (TTA) or frozen after training
signatures.later_use: retrieved by key for later similar actions
signatures.claimed_effect: lower ASR with preserved benign accuracy on Safe-OS/AdvWeb/EIA; competitive on Mind2Web-SC/EICU-AC; transfer across tasks
signatures.failure_boundary: weak backbone unstable to order; learning phase misses early attacks; universal criteria cost 2.7% accuracy

signatures.object: per-check routing between Executor reasoning and external detection tools
signatures.information: safety check text, environment access, tool descriptions
signatures.operation: Executor decides per check whether to invoke OS/permission/HTML tool or reason; tool results join the verdict
signatures.conditions: tools exist for the environment (OS, EHR, EIA HTML)
signatures.persistence: tool definitions fixed; checks that need tools stay in memory
signatures.claimed_effect: catches environment-dependent attacks such as overwrite on rename

assessment.evidence_level_note: A memory built on a Mind2Web-SC train split and frozen improves held-out accuracy over no memory (Claude OOD 93.9±1.0 vs 89.7±1.0, 3 seeds; ID within noise). Narrow: one dataset; main tables and transfer are TTA on the evaluated stream.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: a frozen check memory helps held-out Mind2Web-SC domains for Claude; online-TTA AGrail blocks far fewer benign actions than same-LLM prompt guardrails at low ASR on 20–100-item groups. 'Strong transferability' is not supported as a gain (opus:O03); 'optimal/lifelong' claims are not tested.
unresolved: Table 3 vs Table 9 GPT-4o-mini ID TTA (84.1 vs 74.1; opus:O01–O02).
Whether labels enter memory 'training' is unstated.
No tool-off/Executor-off/budget-matched controls; cost only a figure.

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Fixed component (manually specified trusted contexts / LLM policies) and nearest neighbours (GuardAgent, Conseca) named, with a measured residue (prompt guardrails block up to ~50% benign actions).

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The Analyzer/Executor edit loop, step-back key and per-check tools fit the over-blocking problem, but the key assumption — that the same LLMs can tell necessary from harmful checks without any outcome label — is unexamined, and 'converges to Ω*' is unobservable outside the constructed learning analysis.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Algorithms 1–3, overwrite threshold 0.8 and tool roles given; prompts are images, memory 'training' (labels?) unstated, no versioning, rollback, forgetting or growth control.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55. ASR/accuracy use ground-truth labels and attacks were validated, but the headline agreement metric is judged by Claude-3.5 (an AGrail backbone) with validity asserted, not measured (opus:O05); Safe-OS is a 100-item author-built set scored by keyword matching; benign accuracy is conditional on agent success (opus:O06).

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. No/freeze/TTA memory ablation with 3 seeds on Mind2Web-SC isolates stored checks; no Executor-off, tool-off, nearest-neighbour or budget-matched controls; system baselines are single-call and lack the environment tool.

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with son55. A clean ID/OOD freeze-memory split exists but only on Mind2Web-SC; all main-table numbers and the transfer test are TTA on the evaluated stream, the transfer table shows no gain over the no-transfer base (opus:O03) while the text claims strong transferability (opus:O04), and the ablation numbers disagree between Table 3 and Table 9 (opus:O01–O02).

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 2 (A2 ladder): 3-seed std for memory and order ablations and admitted learning-phase misses; main tables single runs on 20–100-item groups with no intervals.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Only a qualitative input-token figure; no call counts, output tokens, latency or tool-codegen cost despite two LLMs plus tools per action.

The operations fit the problem (sol), but the load-bearing assumption — label-free self-judged pruning finds the right checks — is neither argued nor tested beyond a constructed single-action convergence plot.
